subject: Delivery window exception & dedupe guarantees for AtlasHealth POC
messages:
From: Sara Lopez <sara@atlashealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@atlashealth.com
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Delivery window exception request for AtlasHealth POC

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the demo last week — AtlasHealth is excited about the quality and cost profile on the POC. Before we move forward with ingesting a month of claims data, procurement asked me to confirm if Redwood can make a narrow exception to the async job completion window for this engagement.

Current ask: our ingestion pipelines will submit large daily batches (~18k documents per run) and we need a stronger commitment than the default 24-hour completion window for the POC. Specifically:
- Target: 12-hour completion window for async/batch jobs during the POC period (60 days)
- Visibility: notifications when a job is running beyond 8 hours and a final completion alert at 12 hours
- Deduplication/idempotency: support so that retries (either client-initiated or automatic) do not create duplicate outputs for the same logical payload

We understand this is an exception request — please advise what you need from us (SOW language, test windows, SLAs/credits) and whether Redwood can provide a temporary commitment for the POC. Procurement copied here as procurement@atlashealth.com.

Appreciate a quick confirmation — we are targeting a July 5 start for the full ingest.

Best,
Sara Lopez
Director, Data Partnerships
AtlasHealth

--

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Lopez <sara@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Delivery window exception request for AtlasHealth POC

Hi Sara — thanks for laying this out clearly. We can support a scoped, time-limited exception for the POC with a few guardrails. Looping in Dev (solutions) and Marcus (SRE) to confirm technical feasibility and Laura for contractual language.

High-level proposal (POC, 60 days):
- Completion window: 12-hour end-to-end completion for async batch jobs submitted to the dedicated POC queue.
- Early alerting: automated alert at 8 hours (email + webhook to your monitoring endpoint) and an escalation notice at 10 hours to both teams.
- Idempotency / dedupe: Redwood will enable an idempotency token header and maintain a 72-hour dedupe window for matching keys. For requests without an idempotency key we will fall back to a payload-hash dedupe for 48 hours (best-effort).
- Retries: exponential backoff with a maximum of 5 retries; transient failures will be retried automatically unless client indicates 'no-retry'.
- Remediation: if completion exceeds 12 hours we will provide a one-time credit proportional to the job cost for the POC; exact credit language to be drafted by contracts.

Next steps we need from AtlasHealth:
1) Confirm acceptance of 12-hour window and notification cadence (reply to this thread).
2) Provide any required endpoint for alert webhooks.
3) Sign a short SOW addendum (I’ll share a one-page carveout) — Laura will draft.
4) Allow a quick cross-team test (we’d like to run two representative batches during a 48-hour test window).

I attached our internal retry policy (retry_policy_v2.docx) so you can see the exact backoff we plan to apply. Marcus / Dev — please confirm the dedupe semantics below and flag any constraints.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai

Thanks Hannah — that looks like a good starting point. A couple of clarifications from procurement:

- Can you confirm the webhook payload for the 8-hour alert (we need timestamp, job_id, current_progress, estimated_time_to_completion).
- For dedupe behavior: if we send the same job with two different idempotency keys (client error), which key wins?

If you can confirm those three bullets we’ll sign the SOW addendum and provide the webhook endpoint. We can run the first representative batch July 6 afternoon (PST).

Best,

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Lopez <sara@atlashealth.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 15:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Delivery window exception request for AtlasHealth POC

Hi Sara — quick technical answers below: happy to walk through in a 30-min call.

1) Credits: We can commit to per-job credits for the POC. Contracts will define the credit calculation (we typically use job token cost * multiplier) but per-job is OK.

2) Webhook payload (sample fields):
- job_id (string)
- submitted_at (ISO8601)
- alert_at (ISO8601)
- current_progress (percent)
- estimated_time_to_completion (seconds)
- error_code (if any)
We will provide a sample JSON schema in the SOW addendum.

3) Dedupe / idempotency precedence:
- If two submissions arrive with different idempotency keys but identical payloads, the most recent idempotency key supersedes for dedupe window if the job has not started processing. Once processing begins for a job_id, subsequent submissions are linked to the first started job.
- Recommendation: clients should always supply a stable idempotency key (UUID) per logical batch. If a client sends two different keys for the same logical payload we treat them as distinct attempts unless the payload hash matches an un-started job entry.

Tech notes on implementation:
- Header to use: X-RWI-Idempotency-Key (recommended).
- Server returns: 202 Accepted with job_id + location header for status polling.
- Dedupe windows: canonical dedupe 72 hours for idempotency-key matches; 48 hours for payload-hash-only matches (best effort).
- Retry strategy: exponential backoff (base 2s, max interval 180s), max 5 retries. Automatic retries will not create duplicates if idempotency key is provided.

Operational asks from AtlasHealth before POC run:
- Provide webhook endpoint and a test credential.
- Approve a one-hour test window July 6 (PST) to run two representative batches.

I’ll attach the sample webhook schema and a short runbook to the SOW addendum. Laura, please coordinate the SOW language for per-job credits and notification SLAs.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
